name: Halstrom MA-1 Bomber
description:
A classic MA-1 silhouette in sage-green nylon with an orange reversible lining — a design that has barely changed in two centuries because there was never much reason to change it. Ribbed cuffs, collar, and hem. A single utility pocket on the left sleeve. Halstrom manufactures these in a Milwaukee suburb facility, and the quality control is consistent: every zipper runs smooth, every seam is flat-felled. The fit is slightly relaxed through the body, snug at the wrists.

This is a jacket you see everywhere in Tier 2 and Tier 3. Delivery riders, night-shift techs, warehouse coordinators — anyone who needs something tough, packable, and not too precious to wear in the rain.
what_it_says: Functional and unpretentious. You know what works and you don't overthink it.
story_hooks: Someone left a reversible Halstrom bomber at a crime scene — orange side out — and the only witness says the shooter was wearing it green side out
A counterfeit run of these jackets has been circulating on the Shelf; the fakes are nearly identical but the lining conceals a thin mesh of signal-dampening material
Halstrom's Milwaukee facility just announced a mass layoff — the workers left behind are organizing, and someone is using these jackets as a symbol

physical_description.visual_profile: A timeless MA-1 silhouette with a slightly relaxed cut through the body, creating an approachable, utilitarian presence. The sage-green nylon catches light with a subtle sheen. When the wearer moves or flexes, glimpses of the burnt-orange reversible lining show at the cuffs and collar, adding visual depth. The overall impression is dependable, workwear-adjacent, yet refined enough for mixed social settings.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and shoulders with a tapered waist. Snug at the wrists via ribbed cuffs. The collar sits close to the neck without constriction. Designed to layer over light thermals or augmentation ports without binding.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade nylon, water-resistant but breathable. The fabric has a smooth, slightly matte finish characteristic of mid-tier synthetic textiles.
physical_description.texture: The nylon shell is smooth to the touch with a subtle warp visible under angled light. Ribbed knit at cuffs, collar, and hem provides tactile contrast and grip retention. All seams are flat-felled for durability and comfort against skin or synthetic underlayers.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sage green primary exterior with a burnt-orange reversible lining. No additional patterns or logos—the Halstrom name is subtly woven into the inner collar tag.
physical_description.closures: Full-length zipper with a smooth aluminum pull tab. Friction-fit at the cuffs and waistband via ribbed knit compression.
distinctive_features: Single utility pocket on the left sleeve—large enough for a data-chip wallet or compact tools
Reversible orange lining visible at collar, cuffs, and hem
Ribbed knit collar, cuffs, and hem
Aluminum zipper with consistent glide—no catching
Halstrom's subtle woven tag inside the collar, no ostentatious branding
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3. Accessible to working-class professionals and delivery/logistics personnel. High enough quality to signal reliability and stable employment, not luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by delivery riders, night-shift technicians, warehouse coordinators, and independent couriers across the GLMZ. Signals competence, practicality, and comfort in mixed weather and mixed company. No gang affiliations or subculture markers—the MA-1 transcends social boundaries.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after 3–6 months of wear, with subtle creasing at the elbows and a slight patina on the nylon from rain and sweat. The zipper remains smooth. Patches or reinforcement may appear on the sleeve pocket or cuffs after a year of heavy use, but the jacket is built to accept modifications without losing integrity.
